description: Together, we want to explore the universe, learn new things, and create something truly out of this world! 🚀
summary:
Launch Lab is an interactive web-based training game that teaches players how to survive and operate on the Moon and Mars. Acting as junior astronaut trainees, players explore off-world habitats, complete interactive quizzes, and tackle real mission challenges—from operating Extravehicular Mobility Units (EMUs) and managing life support to surviving abrasive lunar regolith, 120-hour lunar nights, and global Martian dust storms.

Directly powered by official NASA datasets, architectural blueprints, and astronaut training frameworks, Launch Lab bridges the gap between engaging gameplay and authentic aerospace science. Rather than treating mistakes as setbacks, the game uses a trial-and-improvement loop that encourages players to learn from failed attempts, track their progress as they advance from Earth simulations to space habitats, and view difficulty as a stepping stone to success. By transforming complex STEM concepts into an accessible, hands-on adventure, Launch Lab sparks lasting curiosity in space exploration and empowers learners to build the confidence and persistence needed to overcome tough challenges.
details:
Launch Lab is a browser-based STEM game where players prepare a four-person crew, learn about an outpost, and manage a seven-day Moon or Mars mission. Before launch, they complete a 12-stop field guide with NASA imagery and knowledge checks. In the 3D mission, players move astronauts around the outpost, operate equipment, monitor resources, complete 21 daily objectives, respond to a new astronaut scenario each day, and manage five shared challenge lives.

The browser interface sends player actions to the mission logic, which updates resources, equipment, objectives, and mission status. The 3D scene then reflects the game state. NASA photos support the field guide, and recent NASA DONKI solar-flare records power an optional space-weather quiz.

Benefits and intended impact

The project makes spaceflight concepts more interactive and approachable. It encourages players to:

Think about how life-support, power, water, food, and crew decisions affect one another.

Practice interpreting evidence and managing limited resources.

Explore NASA mission results in a hands-on learning context.

The goal is to support curiosity and systems thinking—not to train people for actual missions.

Tools and technology

The main programming language is TypeScript, using React and Next.js for the interface and server routes. Three.js, through React Three Fiber, renders the 3D outpost; CSS styles the interface. The project also uses Node.js, NASA’s Image and Video Library API, NASA DONKI, and NASA science references such as the BVAD. PostgreSQL can provide durable mission saves; local development can use temporary in-memory storage. Docker and Vitest support deployment and testing.

No specialized hardware is required. Players need a modern browser with WebGL support; NASA data and photos require an internet connection.

What makes it creative, and factors considered

Launch Lab combines a walkable 3D outpost, moving crew, daily challenges, a preflight learning guide, NASA imagery, optional sound effects, and MIRA, a draggable mascot that offers hints. The design also considers readability, clear feedback, fallback behavior when NASA images fail to load, and the difference between scientific references and game assumptions.

The simulation is an educational prototype. It does not calculate radiation dose or use live crew dosimetry, live lunar or Martian conditions, OSDR, or RadLab. Game thresholds are not NASA safety limits or operational guidance.
